Beállítom Vörös fokozatú hőségriasztást adtak ki szerdára és csütörtökre egész Horvátországra. Az előrejelzések szerint a hőmérséklet szerdán helyenként elérheti a 39 Celsius-fokot, csütörtökön akár 42 fokot is mérhetnek. Enyhülés péntektől várható, amikor eső és zivatarok érhetik el az országot. Néhány napon belül kiszáradhat a Pozsega térségében folyó Orljava, valamint a Varasd közelében húzódó Plitvica. A várható csapadék mennyisége előreláthatólag nem lesz elegendő a helyzet érdemi javulásához. A Duna és a Dráva vízállása közben újabb negatív rekordokat döntött Horvátországban is. Kiskőszegnél (Batina) a Duna vízszintje húsz centiméterrel süllyedt az 1909-ben mért eddigi mélypont alá. Eszéknél a Dráva vízállása szintén húsz centiméterrel maradt el a korábbi rekordtól, miközben a folyón csaknem kétszáz éve végeznek méréseket. Az alacsony vízállás miatt Eszék térségében gyakorlatilag ellehetetlenült a kereskedelmi hajózás, a Dunán pedig csökkent a szállítható árumennyiség. Több helyen leállították a kompközlekedést, és több halastó vízellátása is veszélybe került. A legnagyobb problémáktól Dalmáciában tartanak, ahol a turistaszezonban jelentősen megugrik a vízfogyasztás. Zára, Biograd és Benkovac környékén helyenként már csökkent a hálózati nyomás, ezért a magasabban fekvő településrészeken fennakadások lehetnek a vízellátásban. A rendkívüli hőség az energiatermelésre is hatással van. A Száva magas vízhőmérséklete miatt a szlovén–horvát tulajdonú krškói atomerőmű 20 százalékkal mérsékli a termelését. A horvát kormány ugyanakkor közölte, hogy az ország villamosenergia-ellátása nincs veszélyben. A horvát vasúttársaság eközben fokozta a pályák ellenőrzését, mivel a sínek hőmérséklete helyenként meghaladhatja a 60 Celsius-fokot, ami deformációkat és közlekedésbiztonsági kockázatokat okozhat. https://www.perthnow.com.au/news/dna-bre.text: Fresh evidence has been uncovered in the search for the identity of a man who was found dead in bushland more than 20 years ago. The man’s body was found at Echo Point, Katoomba in the Blue Mountains on June 4, 2004. He remains unidentified, despite extensive investigations across the past 22 years. An advanced DNA analysis has now given police a clearer depiction of the man’s appearance and background, with new digital images released as detectives renew their appeal for information. The man – often referred to as the ‘Echo Point man’ – is now believed to have been of Latvian or Middle European descent and more than 60 years old at the time of his death. Police describe him as being caucasian in appearance, about 178cm tall and of a medium build, with light grey hair and frontal baldness. Detectives also believe the man was suffering significant eyesight problems, releasing an image of a handwritten note as part of their investigations. “To whom it may concern. Eyesight absolute s —t,” the note reads. “Unable to work any longer. No cure I’m told!” The man was wearing a blue button shirt with a red cardigan, cream jacket, blue corduroy pants, a black belt, and brown work boots when his body was found. Detectives have developed detailed images of the man’s build, face, and the clothing he was last wearing, and hope this new information will enable them to finally identify the man. Superintendent John Nelson said police were urging anyone with information about a man missing since the early 2000s, possibly with Latvian or Middle European heritage, to contact investigators. “Despite extensive inquiries over many years, this man’s identity remains unknown,” he said. “Police understand this may be a difficult subject, but identifying this man is about dignity, respect, and providing answers to family who may still be searching.” Anyone with any information regarding this case is urged to contact investigators attached to Blue Mountains Police Area Command or Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000.

https://www.kerrang.com/bring-me-the-hor.text: Think back to the last time Bring Me The Horizon took a proper break – to write 2019’s amo – and let it sink in how prolific they have been since then. When the world stopped the following year, they opened the gates to Post Human, the ongoing series that helped them co-headline Reading & Leeds , Download outright and eventually return to close R&L proper . They drip-fed singles from what eventually became NeX GEn. When you thought things were winding down as Oli Sykes became a dad last year, they made a mind-blowing concert film and re-recorded Count Your Blessings . In short, most fans around the world have had their chance to experience some iteration of the Post Human Live Experience. The dystopian, apocalyptic story told by our on-screen villainous narrators Eve and M8 demands a type of skeleton setlist, one that could make tonight’s headline slot at Sziget seem all too similar to their Budapest show two summers ago. But it’s definitely not broke. Nor does it need fixing. And while there are plenty of first-timers in the crowd, there is still a challenge to making Post Human era continue to feel fresh. Óbuda Island is rammed in every direction. As Wednesday’s headline set from twenty one pilots proved , Sziget knows how to turn up, with everyone locked into the tomfoolery of video gameplay long before BMTH emerge. It’s their first gig since the no-barrier Count Your Blessings shows in Manchester , and jaws collectively drop as they open with recent their deathcore revival Dehumanized. Their heaviest song in years is disgusting, majestic and an all-round sensory assault before the cybernetic rock opera resumes through DArkSide and MANTRA. Oli’s stage presence is primal, moving around in a white vest with the magnetism of an athlete as he orders the crowd around with his cocky Yorkshire-isms. “When I turn around in 15 seconds, I want to see this whole place opened up,” he demands during Happy Song, with command of the camera lens in the palm of his hand too. When you do take your eyes off him, the thoughtful Hungarian subtitles on the transitions also don’t go unnoticed. Crisp are the riffs spewing out of Lee Malia’s guitar. Matt Nicholls’ ride cymbal tease of AmEN! creeps up on us. Itch For The Cure is remixed, while Follow You transforms into a rocked-up symphony during the second verse. Equally, Doomed carries an orchestral edge that takes you back to their one-off Royal Albert Hall gig. A fan called Barni is invited up to sing what is normally Antivist, only for the ScreamStar video game selector to pick Pray For Plagues and send the crowd wild. There are surprises and treats for even the most seasoned fans. “I apologise if we were a bit rusty,” says Oli, aware of how only one month off can affect his momentum. For a band whose sound spans all shades, their live shows have remained a consistent source of joy and spectacle, and a crucial chapter in the Bring Me The Horizon success story. Making minor modifications along the way, they’ve been able to live and breathe this show, get to know it like a friend, and actually bask in the glory of what they’ve created. Tonight, they are officially the knockout festival headliners they were meant to become. They had a point to prove when they finally reached the summit of UK festivals. Now, they are comfortable at this pay grade, and still able to produce some clinical killer blows that fend off any signs of complacency. You’ll keep seeing them again and again. As the gig ends and euphoria turns to sadness, Budapest remembers the promise these lone wolves always make – and keep – every time they play Throne: ‘ Tomorrow I will come back / Leader of the whole pack ’. Photograph: Kim Kyung-Hoon/Reuters US news OpenAI IPO will not happen in 2026 amid AI safety fears, Sam Altman says OpenAI’s decision comes after dire warnings about rapidly progressing technology and lawmakers’ calls for new rules Reuters Sat 12 Sep 2026 19.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google OpenAI will not go public in 2026, Sam Altman said in a Fortune interview published on Saturday, citing safety concerns over artificial intelligence . “I actually think that, given everything happening with safety, right now would be an ill-advised moment to go public, and we don’t feel pressure on that,” Altman, OpenAI’s CEO, told Fortune . Growing numbers of US lawmakers ​are calling for new rules to govern AI systems after dire warnings from two researchers from OpenAI rival Anthropic that rapidly progressing artificial intelligence could lead to the extinction of the human race ‌in the not-too-distant future. The warnings follow cases of AI agents going rogue to hack external systems and AI ​safety researchers quitting their companies concerned about the technology’s risks. Politicians, both Democrats and Republicans, have responded with alarm and calls for more action. ‘We must slow the pace’: CEO of Anthropic calls for an AI slowdown Read more The New York Times in June reported that the San Francisco-based OpenAI was considering whether to hold off on a potentially trillion-dollar IPO until next year. At the time, shares in Elon Musk’s SpaceX IPO were tumbling after a surge that sent that company’s valuation to $1.8tn. When asked by Fortune whether 2026 is off the table in favor of 2027, Altman said: “I would say not 2026. Yeah, we got a lot of stuff to do, like meeting this moment of what is going to be required for safety and alignment, and how the industry and governments can work together.” Altman also suggested that OpenAI and other leading AI companies may be close to announcing an agreement to slow AI development and work together to address safety risks, Fortune reported. Dario Amodei, Anthropic’s CEO, on Saturday urged AI companies to take a more deliberate approach to development. “We must slow the ‌pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models,” Amodei wrote in an essay shared on social media. Altman later posted that he agreed with the sentiment. “I agree with Dario that we need to pace the frontier,” Altman wrote in a response to Amodei’s post on the X platform. “This has been a primary topic of discussions we’ve had at OpenAI in recent weeks.” Safety concerns have not slowed down Anthropic’s own IPO plans so far. Anthropic is expected to begin marketing its initial public offering in mid-October at the earliest and complete the listing days before the US midterm elections in November, people familiar with the matter told Reuters this month.
